## 1. The audio driver

**Source files (live in the vendor tree):**

- `/home/lawson/openvela/vendor/sifli/boards/sf32lb52/sf32lb52_devkit_lcd/src/bsp_audio.c` (30,135 B) — NuttX audio lower-half (`audio_ops_s`)
- `/home/lawson/openvela/vendor/sifli/boards/sf32lb52/sf32lb52_devkit_lcd/src/bsp_audio_hw.c` (30,084 B) — HAL/AUDCODEC/AUDPRC/DMA layer
- `/home/lawson/openvela/vendor/sifli/boards/sf32lb52/sf32lb52_devkit_lcd/include/bsp_audio.h` — exposes only `sf32lb52_audio_initialize()`
- `/home/lawson/openvela/vendor/sifli/boards/sf32lb52/sf32lb52_devkit_lcd/include/bsp_audio_hw.h` — stage geometry defines

Byte-identical copies are kept as the contest repo's record of the work at `/home/lawson/openvela/contest2026_434_TinyMind/board/sf32lb52_audio/src/` and `.../board/sf32lb52_audio/include/`, replayed by `board/sf32lb52_audio/apply.sh` plus patches `0001`–`0006` in `board/sf32lb52_audio/patches/`.

**Registration — `/dev/audio0`**, in `src/sifli_ap.c:467-497` (added by `patches/0001-sifli_ap-register-audio0.patch`, gated `#ifdef CONFIG_AUDIO`):

```c
  FAR struct audio_lowerhalf_s *audio = sf32lb52_audio_initialize();
  ...
      ret = audio_register("audio0", audio);
```

with the comment at `sifli_ap.c:474-476`: *"audio_register() takes the *name* only: with CONFIG_AUDIO_DEV_ROOT it builds "/dev/" + name (nuttx/audio/audio.c:1808), so passing the full "/dev/audio0" here would register "/dev//dev/audio0" instead."*

**audio_ops implemented**, `bsp_audio.c:141-157`:

```c
static const struct audio_ops_s g_sf32lb52_audio_ops =
{
  .getcaps       = sf32lb52_getcaps,
  .configure     = sf32lb52_configure,
  .shutdown      = sf32lb52_shutdown,
  .start         = sf32lb52_start,
  .stop          = sf32lb52_stop,
  .pause         = sf32lb52_pause,
  .resume        = sf32lb52_resume,
  .allocbuffer   = NULL,          /* M3: DMA-aligned buffers */
  .freebuffer    = NULL,
  .enqueuebuffer = sf32lb52_enqueuebuffer,
  .cancelbuffer  = sf32lb52_cancelbuffer,
  .ioctl         = sf32lb52_ioctl,
  .read          = NULL,
  .write         = NULL,
  .reserve       = sf32lb52_reserve,
  .release       = sf32lb52_release,
};
```

**ioctls.** The lower half handles only two; everything else (`RESERVE`, `CONFIGURE`, `ALLOCBUFFER`, `ENQUEUEBUFFER`, `START`, `STOP`, `FREEBUFFER`, `UNREGISTERMQ`, `RELEASE`) is consumed by the NuttX upper half in `nuttx/audio/audio.c`. `bsp_audio.c:824-847`:

```c
      case AUDIOIOC_GETBUFFERINFO:
        {
          FAR struct ap_buffer_info_s *info = ...;
          /* 16 kHz, 16-bit, mono: 8 KiB is 256 ms per buffer.  Two
           * buffers are enough for the upper-half to double-buffer. */
          info->buffer_size = CONFIG_AUDIO_BUFFER_NUMBYTES;
          info->nbuffers = CONFIG_AUDIO_NUM_BUFFERS;
        }
        return OK;
      case AUDIOIOC_REGISTERMQ:
      case AUDIOIOC_UNREGISTERMQ:
        return OK;          /* handled by the upper-half before reaching us */
      default:
        return -ENOTTY;
```

Note `CONFIG_AUDIO_BUFFER_NUMBYTES` / `CONFIG_AUDIO_NUM_BUFFERS` are **not** set in the `ai_agent` defconfig, so the Kconfig defaults apply: `nuttx/audio/Kconfig:40-52` → `AUDIO_NUM_BUFFERS` default **2**, `AUDIO_BUFFER_NUMBYTES` default **8192**. That makes the staging area 2 × 8192 B = 16,384 B, which is exactly what the serial log prints (`staging 16384 B`). `SF32LB52_AUDIO_STAGE_BYTES` is literally `CONFIG_AUDIO_BUFFER_NUMBYTES` (`bsp_audio_hw.h:66-67`), and `enqueuebuffer` hard-asserts the geometry (`bsp_audio.c`, `enqueue: nmaxbytes=%lu, staging half is %u` → `-EINVAL`), as does the hw start path (`bsp_audio_hw.c:697-701`).

**Rate/format constraints.** Advertised rates are exactly two, `bsp_audio.c:59-64`:

```c
/* Sample rates we actually program: both families derive from the 48MHz
 * XTAL via g_adc_clk_xtal[] / g_dac_clk_xtal[] / g_audprc_div_xtal[].
 * Advertise only these - the hardware layer rejects anything else with
 * -EINVAL, so claiming 8K/44.1K here would contradict configure(). */
#define SF32LB52_AUDIO_SAMPRATES  (AUDIO_SAMP_RATE_16K | AUDIO_SAMP_RATE_48K)
```

`getcaps` (`bsp_audio.c:333-392`) returns `ac_channels = 2` (1 min .. 2 max), `ac_format.hw = 1 << (AUDIO_FMT_PCM - 1)`, and `ac_controls.hw[0] = SF32LB52_AUDIO_SAMPRATES` for both `AUDIO_TYPE_INPUT` and `AUDIO_TYPE_OUTPUT`; `AUDIO_TYPE_FEATURE`/`AUDIO_FU_UNDEF` reports `AUDIO_FU_INP_GAIN`. The hard limits live in `bsp_audio_hw.c:545-558`:

```c
  if (bpsamp != 16 || (nchannels != 1 && nchannels != 2))
    {
      _err("unsupported format: %ubit %uch\n", bpsamp, nchannels);
      return -EINVAL;
    }
  adc_clk = hw_find_adc_clk(rate);
  if (adc_clk == NULL)
    {
      _err("unsupported capture rate %lu\n", (unsigned long)rate);
      return -EINVAL;
    }
```

So: **16 bit only, 1 or 2 channels, 16 kHz or 48 kHz** — 16 kHz mono S16LE is squarely inside the supported envelope. Clock tables: `bsp_audio_hw.c:137-138` (ADC), `:150-151` (DAC), `:159-160` (AUDPRC dividers) — each has exactly the `48000` and `16000` rows.

**How configure is driven.** `sf32lb52_configure` (`bsp_audio.c:402`) reads the request out of `audio_caps_s` — `samprate = caps->ac_controls.hw[0]`, `bpsamp = caps->ac_controls.b[2]`, `nchannels = caps->ac_channels & 0x0f` — and calls `sf32lb52_audio_hw_config_capture(samprate, nchannels, bpsamp)`. Mic gain is set through `AUDIO_TYPE_FEATURE` / `AUDIO_FU_INP_GAIN` with a 0..1000 scale mapped to 0..30 dB (`SF32LB52_GAIN_SCALE_MAX` / `SF32LB52_GAIN_DB_MAX`).

Two driver behaviours a streaming app must live with: the driver is a **single instance** (`reserve()`/`release()` enforce one session; `bsp_audio.c:858-890`), and `pause()` is destructive — `resume()` re-runs the full `config_capture()` (`bsp_audio.c:672-707`, long comment explaining `HAL_AUDPRC_Clear_Adc_Channel` + soft reset).

## 2. How a recording is currently driven

The tool is **NuttX's stock `nxrecorder`**, not a purpose-written app. Enabled by `CONFIG_SYSTEM_NXRECORDER=y` (added by `patches/0004-defconfig-enable-audio.patch`). Source: `/home/lawson/openvela/apps/system/nxrecorder/` (`nxrecorder.c`, `nxrecorder_main.c`, `nxrecorder_common.c`, `nxrecorder_amr.c`). There is no bespoke recorder in the contest repo — `app/` contains only the `hello_app` template.

**Exact NSH command lines.** Default (48 kHz stereo), from `/home/lawson/openvela/contest2026_434_TinyMind/docs/上板验证清单.md:135-137` and `docs/作品介绍文档.md:310-321`:

```
nsh> nxrecorder
nxrecorder> device /dev/audio0
nxrecorder> recordraw /data/test.pcm
nxrecorder> stop
nxrecorder> q
```

16 kHz mono, from `/home/lawson/openvela/contest2026_434_TinyMind/docs/audio-evidence/验证矩阵-0917-8of8.log` (phase C2):

```
recordraw /data/t16k.pcm 1 16 16000
```

Parsed at `apps/system/nxrecorder/nxrecorder_main.c:187-194`: `sscanf(parg, "%s %d %d %d %d", filename, &channels, &bpsamp, &samprate, &chmap)`. 8 kHz is cleanly rejected by the driver in the same log: `sf32lb52_audio_hw_config_capture: unsupported capture rate 8000` → `Error recording file: 22`.

**Output.** Raw headerless PCM, written to tmpfs under **`/data`** (the checklist warns explicitly that `/var` does not exist on this board). Sizes from the AI-agent-firmware regression (`docs/audio-evidence/回归-ai_agent固件-音频未受影响.log`): `933888 regress.pcm`, `745472 regress2.pcm`, both with `sf32lb52_stop: stop: overruns=0`. The `.wav` files in `docs/audio-evidence/` are PC-side reconstructions, not board output (`作品介绍文档.md:405`: board has no file-transfer channel; PCM was exported as serial `hexdump` and rebuilt as WAV on the PC).

**Mechanism: ap_buffer + message queue, not read().** `nxrecorder` opens the device and drives the full upper-half sequence — `AUDIOIOC_RESERVE` (nxrecorder.c:1152), `AUDIOIOC_GETCAPS` (:1170), `AUDIOIOC_CONFIGURE` (:1193), `AUDIOIOC_GETBUFFERINFO` (:1203), `mq_open` (:1221), `AUDIOIOC_ALLOCBUFFER` (:581), `AUDIOIOC_ENQUEUEBUFFER`, `AUDIOIOC_REGISTERMQ` (:1234), `pthread_create` (:1259), `AUDIOIOC_START` (:643) — then loops on `msgrcv`. Each `AUDIO_MSG_DEQUEUE` (:709) writes the buffer out and re-enqueues:

`apps/system/nxrecorder/nxrecorder_common.c:56-63`:
```c
int nxrecorder_write_common(int fd, FAR struct ap_buffer_s *apb)
{
  int ret = 0;
  ret = write(fd, apb->samp, apb->nbytes);
```

`read()` is not a usable path: `ops->read` is NULL, and `nuttx/audio/audio.c` returns 0 immediately — documented in `docs/上板验证清单.md:239`: *"`audio_read` is a空壳, `ops->read == NULL` 时直接 `return 0`… **改用 `nxrecorder`**"*.

## 3. Socket API availability on the `ai_agent` config

`/home/lawson/openvela/vendor/sifli/boards/sf32lb52/sf32lb52_devkit_lcd/configs/ai_agent/defconfig`, hand-appended block at lines 191-249:

```
CONFIG_NET=y
CONFIG_NET_TCP=y
CONFIG_NET_UDP=y
CONFIG_NET_BROADCAST=y
CONFIG_NET_ICMP_SOCKET=y
CONFIG_NET_TCP_WRITE_BUFFERS=y
CONFIG_NET_UDP_WRITE_BUFFERS=y
CONFIG_NET_TCP_DELAYED_ACK=y
CONFIG_NETUTILS_NETLIB=y
CONFIG_NETUTILS_CJSON=y
CONFIG_NETDB_DNSCLIENT=y
CONFIG_NETDEV_LATEINIT=y
CONFIG_SERIAL_TERMIOS=y
CONFIG_EXAMPLES_PPPD=y
CONFIG_NETUTILS_PPPD=y
CONFIG_NET_TUN=y
CONFIG_NET_TUN_PKTSIZE=1500
CONFIG_NETDB_DNSSERVER_NAMESERVERS=1
CONFIG_NETDB_DNSSERVER_IPv4=y
CONFIG_NETDB_DNSSERVER_IPv4ADDR=0xDF050505
CONFIG_IOB_NBUFFERS=64
CONFIG_IOB_THROTTLE=16
CONFIG_NETDEV_IFINDEX=y
```

**UDP and `sendto` are available.** `CONFIG_NET_UDP=y` is on; `CONFIG_NET_IPv4` is not mentioned, so the `nuttx/net/Kconfig:350-352` default `y` applies. `sendto()` exists at `/home/lawson/openvela/nuttx/net/socket/sendto.c` and is compiled whenever `CONFIG_NET` is set, so no new Kconfig symbol is needed for a UDP sender. `CONFIG_NET_UDP_WRITE_BUFFERS=y` means sends are queued to the device rather than blocking on the link.

**No UDP app is currently enabled** — `CONFIG_EXAMPLES_UDP` is absent from the defconfig, and there is no `netlib` UDP helper (`apps/netutils/netlib/` only has `SOCK_DGRAM` uses in `netlib_getroute.c`/`getdevs.c`/`getarptab.c`/`getnbtab.c`, i.e. ioctls, not datagram I/O). The one real UDP socket in the shipped firmware is `/home/lawson/openvela/packages/ai_agent/src/infra/ble_net.c:139` (`socket(AF_INET, SOCK_DGRAM, 0)`), used only to carry a `SIOCGIFMTU` ioctl. Usable patterns to copy, all present in-tree but not enabled: `apps/examples/udp/udp_client.c` (207 lines, `socket(AF_INET, SOCK_DGRAM, 0)` → `sendto` loop, client-side), `apps/examples/udgram/udgram_client.c`, `apps/examples/udpblaster/udpblaster_target.c`.

**The link itself is already proven end to end**, per `/home/lawson/openvela/contest2026_434_TinyMind/docs/AI-Agent端到端实测证据.md`: board side `nsh> pppd /dev/ttyACM0 115200 &`, board gets `ppp0 inet addr:10.0.0.2`, peer `10.0.0.1`, `ping 223.5.5.5` answers in 130 ms, TLS 1.2 handshake OK. So a UDP sender at the board side has a working IP interface to target.

One thing worth flagging for a 640-byte (20 ms) datagram: `CONFIG_IOB_BUFSIZE` is **not** set, so it defaults to **196** (`nuttx/mm/iob/Kconfig:27-31`). A 640-byte payload spans a chain of ~4 IOBs, and the pool is `CONFIG_IOB_NBUFFERS=64` with `CONFIG_IOB_THROTTLE=16`. That is a genuine sizing consideration, not a blocker.

## 4. Free task/heap budget

The 248 KB figure does not appear anywhere. I grepped `docs/` and `README.md` for it — the only hit for "248" in the whole contest repo is a build-progress line in `docs/build-verified.log:302`. The actual documented figures are:

`/home/lawson/openvela/contest2026_434_TinyMind/docs/audio-evidence/ai_agent-反复启停堆占用.log` (three consecutive runs, identical):
```
      total       used       free    maxused    maxfree  nused  nfree name
    8743504    2098576    6644928    2205864    6357184    231     14 Umem
```

`docs/作品介绍文档.md:572` and `:595`:
> 运行期内存 | `free` 报 Umem 总量 **8.7 MB**（512 KB SRAM + 8 MB PSRAM，`CONFIG_MM_REGIONS=2`），PSRAM 已在堆内

> **三次完全一致**，说明这是首次使用后保留的固定结构而非累积泄漏。8.7 MB 总堆中剩余 6.6 MB 可用。

Same document, `:571`: *"资源占用 | flash 13.03%（16 MB）／ sram 29.24%（512 KB）"*.

`docs/AI-Agent端到端实测证据.md:60` (live run after PPP came up): `[agent] Agent loop started, free heap: 8186248`

`docs/演示视频拍摄脚本.md:101`: `[boot +15ms] heap: arena=8743504 free=8330488`

`docs/作品介绍文档.md:545` (audio-only nsh build): *"SRAM 占用 | 88224 B / 512 KB = **16.83%** | 其中 **16 KiB** 为音频双半暂存区（`g_stage`，位于 `.bss`）"*.

**Budget verdict: a 32 KB/s UDP stream is trivially affordable.** That is 640 B per 20 ms frame, 50 datagrams/s — nothing against a 6.6 MB free heap. Task stacks on this build are generous, not tight: `CONFIG_DEFAULT_TASK_STACKSIZE=16096`, `CONFIG_IDLETHREAD_STACKSIZE=16096`, `CONFIG_SYSTEM_WORKQUEUE_STACK_SIZE=32768`, the `ai_agent` builtin itself 32 KB. The only memory-shaped caveats are the IOB pool noted in §3 and the observation at `作品介绍文档.md:697` that `/data` tmpfs stopped growing around 1 MiB (irrelevant for streaming, which writes no file).

## 5. What a minimal PCM→UDP sender would have to touch

**Can it live entirely outside the driver? Yes.** Nothing needed for 16 kHz mono S16LE capture is missing from the existing interface: `/dev/audio0` is registered, `AUDIO_TYPE_INPUT` + `16000` + 16 bit + 1 channel is a hardware-verified configuration (proven on the 8of8 matrix run), and the app-facing contract is the standard NuttX upper-half sequence. **No driver edit is required.** The pieces it reuses as-is:

- `open("/dev/audio0")` + `AUDIOIOC_RESERVE` / `GETCAPS` / `CONFIGURE` / `GETBUFFERINFO` / `ALLOCBUFFER` / `ENQUEUEBUFFER` / `REGISTERMQ` / `START` / `STOP` / `FREEBUFFER` / `RELEASE`
- `struct ap_buffer_s` payloads delivered as `AUDIO_MSG_DEQUEUE` on a `mq_open` queue — the same loop `apps/system/nxrecorder/nxrecorder.c:709-760` runs, except the payload goes to `sendto()` instead of `write(fd, ...)`
- `socket(AF_INET, SOCK_DGRAM, 0)` + `sendto()` against the already-working PPP interface (10.0.0.2 → 10.0.0.1)

**What would be new:**

1. One new source file — the capture thread (open/configure/start, `msgrcv` loop, copy `apb->samp`/`apb->nbytes` into a datagram, re-enqueue) plus a small `UdpSender` header if split. Essentially `nxrecorder_write_common()` with `sendto` in place of `write`.
2. A way to launch it. Two precedents exist in-tree, both cheap:
   - **Board-local (smallest):** `vendor/sifli/boards/sf32lb52/sf32lb52_devkit_lcd/src/CMakeLists.txt` already calls `nuttx_add_application()` for `md5_test.c` (lines 57-66, gated `if(CONFIG_CRYPTO)`). One `.c` file plus one `nuttx_add_application` block = **1 new file + 1 edited file**. Gating is the wrinkle: the board's `vendor/sifli/boards/sf32lb52/sf32lb52_devkit_lcd/Kconfig` is a **0-byte file**, so a new symbol would have to be added there (or the app gated on an existing symbol).
   - **Contest-app shape:** the `app/hello_app/` template (`contest2026_434_TinyMind/app/hello_app/`) shows the 5-file form — `*_main.c`, `CMakeLists.txt`, `Kconfig`, `Make.defs`, `Makefile` — mapping to `packages/demos/contest2026_000_hello_app`. That is 5 new files plus a defconfig line.
   - If instead the sender should be an agent tool rather than an NSH command, `patches/0006-ai_agent-board-tools.patch` shows that pattern exactly: new `src/tools/tool_board.c` + `tool_board.h`, one line in the package `CMakeLists.txt`, one include + registration block in `src/tools/tool_registry.c` — 2 new files, 2 edited, inside `packages/ai_agent`.
3. A defconfig insertion in `configs/ai_agent/defconfig` for the new gate symbol (or `CONFIG_NSH_BUILTIN_APPS`-style registration via `nuttx_add_application`, which uses the existing `CONFIG_BUILTIN=y` / `CONFIG_NSH_BUILTIN_APPS=y` already set at lines 68 and 136).

**Design constraints already baked in that the app must respect** (not new work, but load-bearing): single-session device (a streaming app excludes `nxrecorder` and any other audio user for the duration), fixed 8192-B × 2 buffer geometry, and the app thread must keep draining the message queue — the driver defers `AUDIO_CALLBACK_COMPLETE` onto `LPWORK` precisely because a full app queue blocks `file_mq_send` at `CONFIG_AUDIO_BUFFER_DEQUEUE_PRIO` (default 1); see the long explanation at `bsp_audio.c:573-600`. `sendto` on a `CONFIG_NET_UDP_WRITE_BUFFERS=y` socket queues rather than blocking, so a single thread doing capture-drain + send is viable.

One naming note that a future app should be aware of (already logged as known debt at `作品介绍文档.md:704`): the ecosystem convention is `/dev/audio/pcm0c` + `/dev/audio/pcm0p`, and `packages/ai_agent/include/agent_config.h:351-355` still defaults `AGENT_AUDIO_CAPTURE_DEV` to `/dev/audio/pcm0c` / `AGENT_AUDIO_PLAYBACK_DEV` to `/dev/audio/pcm0p` — neither path exists on this board, which is why the agent's own `src/voice/voice_channel.c:688` / `:1056` capture/playback path is unwired. A new streaming app talking to `/dev/audio0` sidesteps that entirely.
